item.title: Regularization Independence in the One-Dimensional Schr\"odinger Equation with Delta Potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.14843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a class of regularizations $\{\delta_\varepsilon\}$ of the Dirac delta defined by a uniform $L^1$ bound, the normalization $\int\delta_\varepsilon\to1$, and a truncated first-moment condition, with no restriction on sign, shape, support, or scaling. For this class we prove that the transmission and reflection coefficients for the Hamiltonian operator $H_\varepsilon=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-\lambda\delta_\varepsilon$ at fixed energy converge to those of the delta interaction. Under the additional assumption that each $\delta_\varepsilon$ is bounded, we show that any family of negative eigenvalues of $H_\varepsilon$ bounded away from zero converges to $-\lambda^2/4$ when $\lambda>0$, and that no such family exists when $\lambda<0$. Both convergences are obtained with an explicit rate, expressed through two integrals of $\delta_\varepsilon$, directly computable for a given regularization. The bound-state convergence follows from the work of Brasche, Figari, and Teta; here, our contribution is an elementary proof with an explicit rate. Their norm resolvent convergence, however, does not by itself imply convergence of the scattering matrix, which was previously known for families obtained by scaling a single fixed profile; we prove it for a strictly larger class.
item.dc:creator: Alex Czemerinski, Jonathan Nunes, Sergei V. Shabanov

item.title: Strict Monotonicity of the First Positive Steklov Eigenvalue on Eccentric Spherical Shells in Every Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.15063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $d\ge2$, consider the region between two nested spheres of fixed radii, with the inner sphere translated a distance $\varepsilon$ from the outer center. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Steklov problem, with the spectral boundary condition imposed on both spheres, decreases strictly with $\varepsilon$ throughout the noncontact interval. This settles the planar monotonicity conjecture formulated by Nigam and establishes its higher-dimensional counterparts. In dimension two we use a double-center holomorphic expansion and a pair of positive compact coefficient operators. For every $d\ge3$, solid Gegenbauer harmonics yield analogous axisymmetric and transverse operators, with a positive rank-one monopole correction. Weighted angular-mode comparison for $d\ge3$ and a direct matrix comparison for $d=2$ identify the first positive eigenvalue as the unique level-one crossing of an associated spectral radius. The first eigenspace has dimension $d$ in the concentric case and dimension one for every nonconcentric configuration. Convergence and reconstruction estimates justify the coefficient reductions at the two boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Huaian Diao, Jinrui Zhang

item.title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
item.description: arXiv:2611.15180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].
item.dc:creator: David Krejcirik, Petr Siegl

item.title: The P\'{o}lya--Szeg\H{o} buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
item.description: arXiv:2611.15243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} buckling conjecture in dimensions $2\le n\le47$: among open sets of prescribed finite volume, a ball minimizes the first clamped buckling eigenvalue. More precisely, we establish the sharp comparison $\Lambda_1\left(\Omega\right)\ge \left(j_{n/2,1}/j_{n/2-1,1}\right)^2 \lambda_1^{\mathrm D}\left(\Omega\right)$, where $\lambda_1^{\mathrm D}$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and $j_{\nu,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$ of the first kind. The proof extends a radial calibration to all Hessian directions; positive coefficient expansions and logarithmically convex Laplace integrals control the resulting matrix. A Lipschitz construction handles sign changes and arbitrary boundaries. Equality in the volume bound holds precisely for balls modulo sets of zero $H^2$ capacity. We prove that this calibration fails in every dimension $n\ge48$.
item.dc:creator: Guowei Dai, Yingxin Sun, Yong Zhang

item.title: Counting eigenvalues below the lowest Landau level Robin Dirichlet boundary conditions in an annulus
item.description: arXiv:2611.15775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a charged quantum particle confined to an annulus and subject to a strong uniform magnetic field. A Dirichlet condition is imposed on the inner boundary and a Robin condition on the outer boundary. We are interested in the number of bound states whose energy lies below the lowest Landau level, the threshold set by the magnetic field in the whole plane. In the semiclassical regime, we derive an asymptotic formula for this number. It shows how the count depends on the geometry of the annulus, through the length and curvature of the outer boundary, and on the strength of the Robin parameter. We treat both the repulsive and the attractive cases of the Robin condition and describe how the attractive case changes the boundary behavior that produces these low-lying states. The proof reduces the problem to an effective one-dimensional model near the outer boundary and relies on separation of variables in angular momentum.
item.dc:creator: Marwa Nasrallah, Iman Almoustafa

item.title: Counting circles in Kleinian circle packings
item.description: arXiv:2611.16328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a bounded Kleinian circle packing with symmetry group $\Gamma$, and let $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ denote the number of circles in $\mathcal{P}$ of radius at least $T^{-1}$. We obtain an asymptotic formula for $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ in which the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator below the continuous spectrum contribute a finite sum of main terms, with an error term having the same exponent as in the counting theorem of Lax--Phillips for $\Gamma$-orbits in $\mathbb H^3$.
item.dc:creator: Samuel C. Edwards

item.title: Sharpness of the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent for the integrated density of states
item.description: arXiv:2611.15014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent $1/(2\omega)$ for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer $k$ and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree $k$ such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is $k$, and the exact local H\"older exponent is $1/(2k)$. In particular, the $1/2$-H\"older regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime. The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration that adjusts the potential coefficients to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix. A comparison with an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization then reduce the IDS estimate to a two-dimensional rotation-number estimate.
item.dc:creator: Jiabo Ye, Jiangong You

item.title: Quantum unique ergodicity and the critical crossover for 1-d Gaussian band matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.15085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider an $N\times N$ complex Gaussian random band matrix in one dimension with band width of order $W$, in the periodic block form of Yau and Yin. The $N$ sites are split into $n=N/W$ blocks of size $W$ on a ring, and the entries are nonzero only within a block and between adjacent blocks. The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\to\tau\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $\tau\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $\tau\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Promit Ghosal, Guillaume Remy

item.title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.15400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.
item.dc:creator: Zixuan Qiu, Pengshuai Shi, Ruijun Wu

item.title: Generic equivariant simplicity of the spectrum of Laplace-type operators with finite symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.15832v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for generic elements in three natural families of Laplace-type differential operators on smooth manifolds, which are equivariant with respect to a finite symmetry group, all the eigenspaces are irreducible representations. In other words, the spectrum of these operators is generically equivariantly simple. The three families of operators with symmetry are Schr\"odinger operators parametrized by the potential, going back to the work of Wigner, Laplace-Beltrami operators parametrized by invariant Riemannian metrics and conformal Laplacians parametrized by invariant metrics in a given conformal class. The latter two results extend prior work of Zelditch for certain free group actions and resolve, for finite group actions, a well-known open question raised by Guillemin and Yau. Our approach stems from methods developed by Wendl and Doan-Walpuski to address equivariant transversality in symplectic topology.
item.dc:creator: Egor Morozov, Egor Shelukhin

item.title: Polarity of the First Dirichlet Liouville Spectral Gap
item.description: arXiv:2611.16432v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove zero $1$-capacity of first-gap collisions for the minimal Liouville spectral Green-response form and its canonical extension. The minimal-form diffusion avoids collisions for every initial law absolutely continuous with respect to the spectral law.
item.dc:creator: Chunhao Cai

item.title: On the Hausdorff measure of sets of non-Lyapunov behaviour, and a Jarnik-type theorem for random Schroedinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2112.14662v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the growth of the norms of transfer matrices of ergodic discrete Schr\"odinger operators in one dimension. It is known that the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is slower than prescribed by the Lyapunov exponent is residual in the part of the spectrum at which the Lyapunov exponent is positive. On the other hand, this exceptional set is of vanishing Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is integrable at zero. Here we show that this condition on $\rho(t)$ can not in general be improved: for operators with independent, identically distributed potentials of sufficiently regular distribution, the set of energies at which the rate of exponential growth is arbitrarily slow has infinite Hausdorff measure with respect to any gauge function $\rho(t)$ such that $\rho(t)/t$ is non-increasing and not integrable at zero. The main technical ingredient, possibly of independent interest, is a Jarn\'ik-type theorem describing the Hausdorff measure of the set of real numbers well approximated by the eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator. The proof of this result relies on the theory of Anderson localisation and on the mass transference principle of Beresnevich--Velani.
item.dc:creator: Sasha Sodin

item.title: Eigenvalue estimates of the drifted Cheng-Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2107.09135v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish universal eigenvalue inequalities for a drifted Cheng--Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Our approach combines a universal quadratic eigenvalue inequality for operators in divergence form with a Rauch-type comparison theorem and a Bochner-type formula. We evaluate the geometric terms in this quadratic inequality under suitable assumptions on the radial behavior of the coefficient tensor and the drifting function, together with curvature pinching conditions. In the general setting, we establish a Rauch-type comparison theorem for the Cheng--Yau operator and derive two auxiliary estimates from its Bochner-type formula. We then prove integral estimates of independent interest and apply them to obtain the desired eigenvalue inequalities for both the Cheng--Yau operator and the drifted Laplacian, recovering known inequalities for the Laplacian. We also establish a rigidity result for the Cheng--Yau operator on a class of bounded annular domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds. In Euclidean space, this result can be applied, for instance, with the potential function of the Gaussian shrinking soliton. The hyperbolic space is treated separately in two settings, one exploiting the conformal relation between its metric and the Euclidean metric, and the other via its warped product structure, reducing the problem to one dimension. We extend the hyperbolic construction of the fundamental gap for the Laplacian to a class of operators in divergence form. Examples are provided to illustrate the scope and applicability of our results.
item.dc:creator: J\'ulio C. M. da Fonseca, Jos\'e N. V. Gomes

item.title: Optimizing the ground state energy of the three-dimensional magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2504.21597v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper concerns the shape optimization problem of minimizing the ground state energy of the magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field among three-dimensional domains of fixed volume. In contrast to the two-dimensional case, a generalized "magnetic" Faber-Krahn inequality does not hold and minimizers cannot be balls when the magnetic field is turned on. An analysis of the problem among cylindrical domains reveals geometric constraints for general minimizers. In particular, minimizers must elongate with a certain rate along the direction of the magnetic field as the field strength increases. In addition to the theoretical analysis, we present numerical minimizers which confirm this prediction and give rise to further conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Baur

item.title: Foundational Analysis Of The Solvability Complexity Index
item.description: arXiv:2603.18955v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Solvability Complexity Index (SCI) provides an extensional limit-height formalism for recovering a target map $\Xi$ from finite samples of an evaluation interface $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb C^\Omega$ by finite-height towers of pointwise limits. We first give a foundational analysis of what this extensional framework does and does not determine. In second place, we give a concrete non-trivial bridge result from a comparable SCI object to the well known limit rank of Weihrauch theory.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sorg

item.title: Orthonormal bases of spherical harmonics with maximal Lp norm growth
item.description: arXiv:2609.14023v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we show that for every p>2, there is an orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics on the n-dimensional unit sphere which achieves the maximal Lp norm growth. More precisely, one basis achieves this growth for p up to the critical exponent 2(n+1)/(n-1), and another for p from the critical exponent up to infinity. The first basis is built from rotations of the real part of a highest weight spherical harmonic. The second is built from zonal harmonics whose poles are selected from a spherical design. In both cases, the selection uses the restricted invertibility theorem of Bourgain and Tzafriri. This extends earlier results of Bourgain and of the author (arXiv:1404.5016) on the 2-dimensional sphere for 2<p<=6 to all dimensions and all p>2, and improves the positive density subsequence there to a whole basis.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Han
